diagnosticLimits: Role, owner relation and parent tag describe an earlier PID inventory snapshot with identityBound=false. They do not prove the generation, owner or type at the later denied task query.

systemPsObserved is a count of inventory occurrences, not unique process generations and not proof that a live ps was measured at the task-query instant. Confirmed-gone or later-replaced members can still have appeared in an earlier inventory.
differentOwnerObserved counts owner-relation inventory occurrences; it is not a proof that a particular denied task had that owner.

psTaskDeniedSamples is derived from bounded examples (up to three per snapshot) and is a lower bound. Zero does not exclude ps-related permission denial. Multiple matching denied tasks within one attempt count as one attempt.
A recovered partial permission failure remains diagnostic evidence while a subsequent complete sample may allow progress under unchanged existing retry policy.

Exact Popen child exit code is the monitored worker/suite leader code; it is distinct from a browser or Shim exit code. Reaping this child does not prove all group members or native processes were cleaned up.
A successful short census preflight cannot establish browser startup, native Shim authentication, historical cause-host-exited root cause, or the absence of a rare later permission race.

staticChecks.assessment: Only fixed role values system-ps/system-open/other, same/different owner relations, random-key opaque parent/PID tags and counts are serialized. Raw comm, argv, paths, UID/RUID/PPID are not published by the new metadata fields. identityBound is explicitly false.
staticChecks.subject: Public inventory allowlist

staticChecks.assessment: Every valid PID in the selected PGID still reaches read(pid, pgid). No role/owner exclusion is added. Original libproc identity/birth/state/membership/counter checks and permission early return remain unchanged. EPERM totals stay null, unknown is retained, and no measurement/gone/signal decision uses supplemental ps metadata.
staticChecks.subject: Selection and measurement remain fail-closed

staticChecks.assessment: A valid PGID/PID with missing extra owner/comm metadata still uses the original task query and can be measured. metadataUnavailable cannot itself create a monitor failure. Malformed actual target PID remains unknown.
staticChecks.subject: Metadata absence is diagnostic only

staticChecks.assessment: Probe/signal OSError diagnostics keep operation, signal, error type and errno without exception text; denial is re-raised and not converted to gone. groupCleanup starts unverified after launch and reaches verified-gone only after normal group cleanup succeeds. The exact Popen child independently receives wait(timeout=5) even after group EPERM. Reaped/still-running/unavailable child status does not change unverified group status. No additional signal or privilege is added.
staticChecks.subject: Cleanup group and exact child are distinct

staticChecks.assessment: Four pinned harness file hashes are verified before import/use. The worker executes HostProcess._process_rows all-PID and single-PID calls and the ShimMonitor PID enumeration command, each 12 times, retaining inherited worker PGID. Each loop pauses 0.25 seconds; this is not a guaranteed 30-second workload. No SDK, browser, Shim authentication, build, permission, signing, or session-selection change is performed.
staticChecks.subject: SDK-free representative workload

staticChecks.assessment: Mac pass additionally requires at least two complete samples and system-ps observed in an inventory. Missing ps fails with census-system-ps-not-observed. Recovered and final-failure partial inventory summaries are retained. Final failed attempt is counted once, rather than once as final activity plus once as partial.
staticChecks.subject: Observation coverage and retry retention

staticChecks.assessment: Existing job limit, disk/log/memory guards, owned-native registry and signal sequence are retained. This change adds diagnostics and a bounded exact-child wait; it does not relax EPERM, ownership validation, API access, OS protection, entitlements, retention, authentication or token permissions.
staticChecks.subject: Resource/ownership/permission controls
